title: On Chasing the Rainbow of Intrinsic Motivation
author: Rebecca Birch
summary: Teachers should focus on identified motivation—explicitly communicating the importance of learning and the value of effort—rather than chasing intrinsic motivation, which is unrealistic for most subject teachers. Schools can cultivate identified motivation and integrated motivation (the sense that effort defines who we are as a class) through explicit value communication, aspirational culture, and conditions for competence via structured teaching and unconditional positive regard.
points: Intrinsic motivation is a pipe dream for most subject teachers; identified motivation—explicit communication of importance—is more fruitful through structured teaching.
Integrated motivation, the sense that effort and persistence define us, is within a school's power to influence and more reliable than intrinsic motivation.
When extraneous cognitive load is high and intrinsic load not optimized, students switch off; cognitive load and motivation should be studied together.
Schools should provide conditions for students to thrive through structured teaching, disciplinary environments, practice opportunities, unconditional regard, and explicit enthusiasm.
Teachers modeling enthusiasm and providing learning rationales show school is worthwhile, creating the foundation for identified and integrated motivation.
quotes: Like many peers teaching compulsory subjects, I've learned my enjoyment of reading may not be teachable; we have responsibility to equip students to access knowledge.

Intrinsic motivation has long been the holy grail; but it's a pipe dream for most subject teachers—communicating the value of knowledge is more fruitful.” “As adults with New Year's resolutions know, intrinsic motivation is unrealistic; instead, communicating value and importance will be more fruitful for teachers.
When extraneous load is high and intrinsic load not optimized, students switch off, aligning with Kalyuga's Expertise Reversal Effect.

Rather than trying to motivate, we should provide conditions for students to thrive: supporting competence through structured teaching and environments where everyone can learn.” Archived from Rebecca Birch Substack on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
